rv.q: Its adaptation into a monologue rarely gets an outing, perhaps because it is so bleak, but is staged by the Berliner Ensemble with heaps of extra angst for good measure. It is dramatised with great anguished physicality by Jens Harzer and spoken in German with English surtitles.
You’ll be on the edge of your seat with first-row access to an actor’s career high.
This allows him to shake off the despairing thought of “an appalling ending” and instead say “what a wonderful beginning!”.
The Berliner Ensemble have stripped Wilde’s halo of Sebastian Melmoth dimensions and given him back his indignity; and indignation.
Achingly beautiful as well as briskly shocking, De Profundis stands as one of the great artistic and philosophical works of the Victorian age.
This is a superb production with huge impact, truly achieving the Berliner Ensemble’s objective of making the audience think but also feel deeply.
